title: Cap. 6 Arg. 8 Secundo: Augustine—who are made sheep; no decree to give all the grace that makes believers
pass_a_gloss: The second testimony of Augustine is held in book 4 Against Two Letters of the Pelagians, chapter 6: He who makes human beings sheep himself frees human wills unto the obedience of piety. But why he makes these human beings sheep, and does not make those, is itself the question which belongs to that depth which the Apostle, wishing to look through, shrank back from and exclaimed, O the depth. In these words, by making sheep and not making, nothing else is signified than making faithful and obedient, and not making. Both are attributed to God, and that according to the purpose of his hidden will. Therefore by the death of Christ there has not been established such a decree as some have invented, concerning preparing, offering, and giving to all human beings that grace by which they are rendered believers and obedient, under the condition of free choice embracing the same.
pass_b_english: Augustine's second witness is Against Two Letters of the Pelagians 4.6: the One who makes people sheep is the One who frees human wills for the obedience of piety. Why he makes these sheep and not those—that is the question that belongs to the depth the Apostle feared to look into and cried, [[O the depth >> Bible:Romans 11:33]]. Making sheep or not making them means nothing but making people faithful and obedient—or not. Both acts are God's, and both run by the purpose of his hidden will. So Christ's death did not fix the decree some invent: that the grace which makes believers and the obedient is prepared, offered, and given to everyone, on condition that free choice embrace it.
source_text: Secundum testimonium Augustini habetur lib. 4. contra duas Epist. Pelag. cap. 6: Qui facit oves homines, ipse ad obedientiam pietatis humanas liberat voluntates. Sed quare istos homines oves facit, et istos non facit, ipsa est quaestio quae ad illam pertinet altitudinem, quam perspicere volens Apostolus expavit, et exclamavit, O altitudo. Hisce in verbis per facere oves, et non facere, nil aliud significatur, quam facere fideles et obedientes, et non facere. Utrumque Deo tribuitur, idque secundum propositum arcanae suae voluntatis. Christi ergo morte non est stabilitum tale decretum, quale nonnulli finxerunt, de praeparanda, offerenda et donanda omnibus hominibus ea gratia qua credentes et obedientes reddantur, sub conditione liberi arbitrii eandem amplexantis.
